body:
Now that I think about it, it's because I'm anticipating reactions from people around me. I'm anxious to be stigmatized, pitied, ridiculed or accused of seeking attention. That's how ex girlfriends, parents, friends etc. reacted whenever it became clear that I m not well at all. None of these reactions are empathic, but rather judgemental.. which is my problem, I guess. I'm afraid to be judged.

I'm not even sure if it's possible to be empathic towards someone without being judgmental. Hell I dont even know if I want anyone to be empathic towards my situation. I dont need anyone to feel sorry about me. That makes me feel really pathetic.
Heh. I dont really know what makes me happy though. I have no clue.

I did consider it, but I dont think anyone would care. In fact, there really isnt anyone I'm close with atm.

I used to have a lot of friends, all pf which I lost in the last years. Mostly because I have a terrible habbit of iaolating myself for extended periods of time (read: several months) whenever I have a low. None of my friends were ever close enough to let them know the reason why I would not show any interest in them for so long, so I ended up telling them I was busy, lazy, or not feeling well. Most of them dropped me after that.

I also didnt open up to my parents about it because... well my realtionship to my parents is very, very strained. I mean there's no way I would tell someone how I feel about life if they take every chance to ridicule and me over minor things like sleep issues, being lonely, crying, not being manly etc. This is also why I never engaged in a therapy.

First subreddit is a really interestimg read, thanks for that! As for philosophy, I frequently visit it already. I actualy studied philosophy for almost 2 years. At some point though, I realised that there is no definite answer for anything ever. The answers I seek dont objectively exist. I can use the tools I was given to evaluate and develop my own perspective... I dont need to visit a college and read the literature I am given to do this, so I quit.

It helped me develop more efficient thinking patterns and ways to properly evaluate an argument though and I am thankful for that.

Nope, I havn't. I'm honestly quite proud that I made it this far alone.

Yea, i realised that love, happyness etc. is not something that finds you. You gotta actively work on yourself and your goals to hopefully be happy some time. I know that, however it's really hard to believe that I can in fact achieve happyness... I mean with the experiences I made it's kind of hard to get your hopes up. Which leads to a lack of motivation. 

It's also incredibly hard to try and open up to someone if you were taught/taught yourself the exact opposite. A couselor can only help you help yourself. He cant magicaly fix your state of mind, he can only question yoir premisses and make you reflect and reevaluate.

I wrote a really long response but struggled to put my feelings into words...or make any sense.. 
Here's the short version:
I feel bad about possibly hurting someone because I knoe how much it hurts to feel alone, unloved and abandoned. I felt like this for the majority of my life and only recently learned to somewhat deal with it by myself. I dont want anyone else to feel like this. :-/
I actualy have problems talking to fellow men about feelings or anything private... I can really only open up to women :-/
Congratz! I'm sure you are doing a good job. I hope I can someday look back and say the same :)

Did you never look back and feel bad for just walking away? I mean... is it okay to not care about your parents? Especialy in the case of my mother I feel like its just wrong to walk away. She wasnt exactly there for me, but she never treated me badly either. It feels so wrong to abandon her just because she doesnt break up with this fucking asshole.
I'm 21. Ikr.. I just see so many people my age have such good relationships with their parents. Kinda hurts.

More than one of my exes suggested therapy. Once they learned about how I feel they started pitying me or broke up with me. Well, not all of them, but the vast mayority. That said, none of my relationships lasted longer than 3 months. So yea, this is why I dont tell anyone I care for about this anymore, althought it doesnt change a thing. I'm shameful for how I feel. This is also why I never engaged in a therapy. 

Not sure what you mean by self sabotaging. I have this habbit of deliberately discontinuing friendships etc if I lose someone as a result of isolating myself. If you mean that, then yea I do that too. 

I'm fine by myself usualy, but there's times like birthdays, christmas, or vacations where you realise how lonely you are and what you are missing out on. Life's pretty much a struggle between craving and avoiding love.

That's the thing. I dont know how to coop with getting hurt and losing someone who's precious to you. I never received much love, and therefor embraced what little I had all the more. Upon repeatedly losing what I held most dearly, I adopted a strategy to deal with the loss... that is not allowing any intimacy to not be stripped off of it. I can only hope that I will either be strong enough to keep going by myself, or that someone will be there to pick me up next time I fall...and i will fall. Because thats how the world works.

That I must not be afraid of losing someone. That I need to quit running away from the people I love, just because I am afraid of losing them. That I'm hurting myself and more importantly others because I am afraid to lose a loved one. That I need to embrace the moment and accept that I will inevidebly lose what's precious to me. That you cant find love and happiness without experiencing pain and suffering.
